notes:
The first batch from this source: every San Francisco listing certified before 1980, on the NPS Form 10-300 and its 10-900 successor. 54 nominations, of which 30 are for a building at a numbered street address; the rest are ships in the Maritime collection, objects, military reservations and the two ferry buildings, which the register files by landmark rather than by number.

The batch's own discovery is that **the address the NPS index carries is not always the address the nomination describes**. Nine of these ten 1973 listings are Western Addition Victorians the Redevelopment Agency bought and physically moved rather than demolished during project area A-2, and the index carries the address they were moved *to* while the form's own "street and number" is where they stood when it was written. That is two facts on two different parcels, and both are recorded here.

Owners are left out throughout, per the module's privacy limits: these nominations name the original owner of nearly every Victorian in the 1973 group, and none of those names is a builder, an architect or a firm. Architects, builders and contractors are kept.

coverage.remaining: 111 of the 165 San Francisco listings in the NPS index are certified 1980 or later and are unread; they break into 1980-1989 (42), 1990-1999 (17), 2000-2009 (22), 2010-2015 (15) and 2016-2023 (15). Two documents inside this batch's own date range are also outstanding: 77000334, the Mills Building and Tower, whose PDF is an image-only scan with no text layer, and 78000757, the San Francisco Civic Center district (1978), which is fetched but not read — it is a 99,000-character district nomination naming many buildings and is the obvious next batch.
coverage.note: Read 54 nominations — every San Francisco listing certified before 1980, plus the Civic Center district fetched and left for the next batch. 30 name a building at a numbered street address; 53 of the 54 PDFs carry a usable OCR text layer and one (77000334) does not. 55 findings came out of the 30, plus one stub for the unreadable document.
